title: A colliding preflight removes the other invocation’s worktree after its own add fails
expected: Each proof invocation removes only a worktree it successfully created and owns; concurrent proof of the same commit cannot remove another invocation’s directory.
actual: proveCommit derives preflight-<first12SHA> without a nonce or ownership lock. The finally block always force-removes that directory, including when its add failed because the first invocation already owns it. An owned real-Git fixture runs the second same-SHA invocation while the first is in its callback: second add throws, its finally removes the first directory; first callback observes it gone.
rootCause: Predictable shared directory plus unconditional cleanup without a creation/ownership guard.
impact: Disrupts an ongoing candidate proof and can remove files that the other invocation is still using. Git index/worktree metadata is affected only in the owned fixture; no shared/user worktree was touched.
recommendation: Use a unique invocation directory and remove only after successful owned creation, or hold a per-proof ownership lock through creation/proof/removal. Preserve the original failure. Add concurrent identical-SHA coverage.

verification.method: unmodified production function with real Git in private owned repository and deterministic nested contender
verification.result: outer directory existed before second call and was absent afterwards; outer fake proof returned no failures; actual install intercepted once

relationship: New cause; not RECLAIM-02 expected-tip classification/deletion race. This deletes a proof directory that the contender never owned.
Not a claim that ordinary different-SHA proofs collide.
limits: No real proof command, dependency install, network, provider, publication or user ref. Nested synchronous call models a second process while outer proof is active. Expected Git collision/not-a-worktree messages are retained in stderr; probe itself exits0.
status: confirmed within explicit own local fixture and source boundary
regressionTest: Two proof invocations for identical commit: second failure cannot remove first owned directory; different SHA and add-failure-before-creation controls.

title: Namespace maintenance can classify one remote’s tip and delete a different remote’s branch
expected: A maintenance pass targeting remote origin classifies origin’s advertised/current ref tip; a same-named tracking ref from another remote cannot replace that evidence.
actual: refsUnder gathers refs/remotes/** and coalesces by logical name, allowing every later remote copy to overwrite the earlier one. maintainRefNamespace takes this selected SHA but uses the specified remote for integration/verdict/deletion. Own fixture: origin/pub/audit-fixture has unique work, z-fixture/pub/audit-fixture points at an old ancestor; refsUnder selects the latter, isSpent(selected)=true while isSpent(origin-tip)=false.
rootCause: Remote identity is discarded before choosing the authoritative SHA; “remote wins” is implemented across all remotes rather than the selected maintenance target.
impact: With multiple remotes, eligibility can be based on unrelated old history and downstream reap targets the requested remote, risking removal of its distinct work. The fixture proves wrong selection/classification; it does not execute the downstream delete.
recommendation: Parameterize collection by target remote and keep local/target-remote tips distinct; carry that target SHA into atomic deletion. Unknown target state should be kept, not replaced by another remote.

verification.method: real refsUnder/isSpent with production Git port mapped only to an owned repository
verification.confidence: high for selection/classification; downstream delete traced statically

relationship: Independent of RECLAIM-01 failed-command-as-zero: all commands and SHA reads succeed here but evidence belongs to a different remote.
RECLAIM-02 is separately extended for missing atomic expected-tip consumption; repairing that too prevents the hazardous downstream action.
limits: No real external remote/fetch/push/delete. Synthetic remote-tracking refs exist only in a temporary repo. Single-remote repositories do not meet this demonstrated condition.
status: confirmed within explicit own local fixture and source boundary
regressionTest: Two remotes with same logical branch but divergent tips: only selected remote informs proof; reversed remote ordering and absent selected remote remain conservative.

title: Two initial maintenance contenders can both acquire the lease after observing absence
expected: At most one contender reports successful acquisition of a free lease; observing absence must not authorize deleting a newly linked owner.
actual: Both contenders read no record; the first removes absence, links its record and returns true. The other then executes the unconditional rm based on its earlier observation, removes the freshly acquired lease, links its own record and also returns true. Actual production hold() with legal deterministic fs-port scheduling returns [true,true] and two successful links.
rootCause: A check/remove/link sequence treats “was absent/expired” as permission for an unconditional remove, without tying removal to the observed record or using a separate atomic takeover guard.
impact: Two server processes can initially pass the maintenance gate until a later heartbeat corrects ownership, allowing concurrent background work contrary to the single-maintainer contract. No actual maintenance action was launched by the probe.
recommendation: Acquire free path directly with link without pre-removal; serialize or atomically validate takeover of the exact observed expired record, and fence operations where a changed owner matters. Test first acquisition and expired takeover separately.

verification.method: unmodified lease implementation, actual private files, fs wrappers force a legal read/remove/link interleaving
verification.result: both hold calls true; two links; one of the contenders remains on disk

relationship: New maintenance-lease path; earlier ORCH-03 concerned a different orchestrator lock/TTL.
Source comment already admits transient dual holders on expired takeover. This reproduction starts from absence and shows the same missing-ownership guard even before expiry.
limits: No live process ownership incident claimed, no timers/gates/ref/forge work started. Distinct factory-created lease objects are used in one isolated process; deterministic scheduling represents independent contenders. Convergence at a future beat does not make initial hold results exclusive.
status: confirmed within explicit own local fixture and source boundary
regressionTest: Barrier two free-lease contenders, expired takeover and renewal interleavings: exactly one acquisition; ordinary sequential contender refused until release.

title: Cleanup reports successful deletion after the forge explicitly refuses its branch deletion
expected: Cleanup distinguishes local deletion from a refused remote cleanup and preserves the forge diagnostic/remedy for later completion.
actual: disposeWorkRef forwards expectedSha to the local/remote ports, but ignores the IForgeWriteResult from deleteBranch. A synthetic typed forge port returns ok:false/refused; real cleanup function still returns action:deleted and a reason saying the work ref was deleted. The GitHub adapter itself returns ok:false for refusals, so this is the normal result contract rather than a thrown exception.
rootCause: Awaiting a result is mistaken for checking that it succeeded.
impact: Remote leftovers are described as completed cleanup, reducing observability and potentially leaving a branch to be rediscovered/restored by later maintenance. No work loss is demonstrated by this reporting defect.
recommendation: Consume the forge result and record a partial cleanup/retained-remote outcome including reason and remedy. Keep idempotency for an already-absent branch and test nonthrowing refusals.

verification.method: unmodified disposeWorkRef with synthetic Git/forge ports
verification.result: remote ok:false but returned action:deleted and deletion-success reason; both expectedSha parameters forwarded

relationship: Distinct from RECLAIM-02: result/reporting loss, not absence of expected-tip fencing.
Existing CP-12 concerns settlement boundary; this is the integration cleanup result after a refused remote write.
limits: No actual Git/forge deletion. Local deletion port is synthetic. Does not say the local expected-SHA guard is missing: this source correctly supplies it.
status: confirmed within explicit own local fixture and source boundary
regressionTest: Remote ok:false is reported partial cleanup with reason; remote ok:true succeeds; local expected-SHA refusal remains retained and does not trigger remote cleanup.
